candidates.note: ಕೂಳು is native but lower-register in modern usage; flag this honestly.

DEDR 1911 identifies Kannada kūḻ (ಕೂಳು) ‘boiled rice, food’ as part of Proto-Dravidian *kūḻ ‘porridge’. Tamil kūḻ means thick gruel/porridge; Tulu kūru/kūlu/kūḷu means boiled rice. This is a genuine cognate set, but the meanings range from porridge to boiled rice and food; it should not be treated as an exact synonym for every use of ‘food’.

candidates.note: ನಾಳ್ survives in ನಾಳೆ and compounds; archaic as a free word.

Contributor-supplied candidate; semantic fit and word origin pending editorial review. Comparative evidence: Proto-Dravidian *pakal ‘daylight’; Tamil பகல் (pakal); Telugu పగలు (pagalu); Malayalam പകൽ (pakal); Kannada ಹಗಲು (hagalu), from Old Kannada ಪಗಲ್ (pagal). Tulu shows the p-initial form pagal/pagalu; historical comparative discussion explicitly treats Kannada hagalu as a Kannada h- form and Tulu pagal as the native p- counterpart, rather than treating Tulu hagalu as an inherited cognate. Sources: DEDR 3151; Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras, 1924–1936); historical discussion in Indian Antiquary, vol. 62; comparative Dravidian references.
Contributor-supplied candidate; semantic fit and word origin pending editorial review.
